summary: An agent's description is its charter: up to 8 KiB, shown by agents show and in the restart message

replay.detail: No replay or backfill. Stored declarations are unchanged; the description stays a child of the existing desired declaration body.

schema.detail: No database schema, claim kind, index or migration change. The large-value inventory records the parameterized feature query the declared-admission and charter barriers now share.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules change. Replicated desired-claim admission already treats the declaration body as an opaque object.

compatibility.detail: Native agent declarations, agent.create and the st2 spec path accept a description of up to 8,192 UTF-8 bytes (previously 1,000; agent.create previously 4,096); native descriptions may span lines, st2 descriptions stay one printable line. A member from before this release re-validates declaration KDL with the 1,000-byte rule when it publishes, previews or materializes the agents a mission declares for a run it evaluates (graph.rs validate_agent_body via parse_execution_intent in reconcile materialize_step_declarations and materialize_mission_declarations), although it admits replicated desired claims (intent.desired desired is an opaque object) and reconciles top-level agents from stored declarations without re-parsing. Publishing any declaration, top-level or inside a mission, whose description exceeds 1,000 bytes therefore requires every active fleet incarnation to advertise features.agent_charter=1 in its anchored daemon.started claim, under the declared-admission membership and evidence policy; otherwise the publication or direct intent.desired/mission.published claim fails with agent-charter-feature-barrier before any write. Descriptions of at most 1,000 bytes publish as before. Tests cover the refusal without fleet evidence, refusal when only declared_admission is advertised, publication once agent_charter is advertised, mission-declared agents, and direct claim bodies. The gate checks support at write time only: a member that later runs an older binary refuses or fails to materialize such declarations. The AgentResource wire type is unchanged; agents show reads the description from the existing status read.

downtime.detail: Normal binary restart only. The description is not a launch input, so editing it is publish-only and restarts no seat; the changed st skill text is not part of the launch contract.

manual.detail: To publish a charter over 1,000 bytes, upgrade every active fleet member (or fence legacy peers) first; every active member must advertise features.agent_charter=1, and the gate fails closed without signed, anchored fleet membership, so a standalone member cannot publish one. fractal agents show prints the current declaration's description under Charter; a restarted seat's where-you-were message opens with a Your charter section; the st skill tells a seat to read its charter with agents show when it starts or resumes work. Fractal still sends no message at a seat's first start, and a charter alone does not produce a restart message.

recovery.detail: Before swapping a member back to an earlier release, shorten every description over 1,000 bytes with an upgraded member; the earlier release refuses to republish such declarations and fails to materialize mission-declared agents that carry one. Declarations within 1,000 bytes need no action.
